title: From The Trap Of Geopolitics To A Geo-Civilizational Paradigm | NOEMA
gist: Gardels, drawing on Bruno Maçães' 'In Search Of Greater India,' argues the nation-state is a Western import whose dualistic logic manufactures conflict, and that a 'geo-civilizational' paradigm grounded in Advaita nondualism is the only exit — while conceding India's own 1974/1998 nuclear tests and Pakistan's mimetic response show civilizational wisdom losing to state power.

themes.theme: Nation-state vs. civilization as the organizing unit

insights.claim: The nation-state is framed as a Western export that leaves non-Western polities structurally exposed to Western influence, while civilizational identity is offered as the rival organizing principle for India and China.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A civilizational frame predicts that Indian and Chinese policy will diverge from Western institutional templates rather than converge on them — relevant to long-run sovereign, standards and alliance risk.
insights.quote: “Nation-states are a Western invention, naturally vulnerable to Western influence. Civilizations are an alternative to the West,”

insights.claim: Postcolonial states initially remained inside the imperial mold, and only after becoming strong and prosperous enough to stand alone did China and India reclaim civilizational roots as the guide to building a future in their own image.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Civilizational assertion is a function of accumulated economic power — expect it to intensify, not fade, as these economies grow.

insights.claim: Asserting civilizational identity is only possible through the machinery of the modern state inside an international order whose interests contradict the holism of that civilizational outlook — a built-in contradiction.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Expect rhetoric of civilizational harmony to keep coexisting with hard-power behavior; do not trade the rhetoric.

insights.claim: Civilizations can coexist across boundaries, but conflating claimed universal 'civilization power' with national interests is what makes the world dangerous.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A concrete tripwire for escalation risk: watch for state actors dressing national interest in universalist civilizational language.
insights.quote: “civilizations can coexist across boundaries, but when ‘civilization power’ is claimed as universal and conflated with national interests, the world becomes a dangerous place.”
insights.locator: As the Chinese-Singaporean historian Wang Gungwu

themes.theme: Nondualism as an alternative to good-vs-evil geopolitics

insights.claim: The national ego behaves like Jung's insecure person: it projects repressed traits onto others, converting rivals into repositories of evil and turning world politics into a final confrontation in which annihilation is permanently latent.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A psychological model of escalation: adversary demonization is endogenous, so de-escalation narratives are fragile.
insights.quote: The monsters we confront are the monsters we ourselves have created.
insights.locator: He cites Carl Jung on the unenlightened

insights.claim: Advaita nondualism treats the ego-versus-other opposition as the lowest level of consciousness and personality as a temporary mask, which is presented as the philosophical antidote to dualistic international politics.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Gives the intellectual scaffolding behind India's non-aligned, non-bloc posture — useful for reading Delhi's refusal to pick sides.
insights.quote: In Indian thought, dualism has been repeatedly rebutted.

insights.claim: The Hindu ethical inversion — in Christianity the body has a soul, in Hinduism the soul has a body — makes being good to others identical to being good to oneself, rather than an obligation imposed from outside.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Illustrates why Indian elite discourse resists Western rules-based moralism framed as external constraint.
insights.quote: that whereas in Christianity the body has a soul, in Hinduism the soul has a body. In other words, we are emanations of a universal soul, the atman.
insights.locator: When Shashi Tharoor, the Indian diplomat

insights.claim: A durable world order cannot be built on power itself but only on detachment from power — those who turn the world into hell will have to live in it too.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A normative bet against realist balance-of-power stability; treat as directional worldview, not as forecast.
insights.quote: World order can never be based on power but must grow from the effort to detach ourselves from power and from the world, having experienced its joys but knowing its limits.
insights.locator: Even when conflict resorts to force

insights.claim: Toynbee's binary is invoked as the stakes of the argument: a chapter that began in the West must end either the 'Indian way' or with the bomb.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Frames the whole essay as an existential-risk argument, not an academic one.
insights.quote: will have to have an Indian ending. It will be either the ‘Indian way’ or the bomb.
insights.locator: It is from within this perspective

insights.claim: India tested its first nuclear device in 1974 under the name 'Smiling Buddha,' nearly 30 years after independence, and tested again in 1998 as 'Operation Shakti' — civilizational vocabulary attached to nuclear weapons.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that civilizational framing does not restrain hard-power behavior; discount claims that it will.
insights.locator: Despite the civilizational light of Advaita

insights.claim: After India's 1998 test, Pakistan's then-opposition leader Benazir Bhutto publicly called for a preemptive strike to destroy India's nuclear capacity, and Pakistan conducted its own first test later that same year, becoming the only Muslim-majority nuclear state.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A documented escalation ladder driven by mimetic rivalry — the base case for how South Asian nuclear risk recurs.

insights.claim: Ancient Asian worldviews such as Daoism have been eclipsed at the exact moment their plausibility returns, because the Eastern mind was colonized by the instrumental reason of the Western Enlightenment.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Cautions against expecting Chinese climate or tech policy to follow indigenous philosophical traditions rather than instrumental-rationalist logic.
insights.quote: But in reality, the Eastern mind has been colonized by the instrumental reason of Western Enlightenment, which became globally dominant in recent centuries.

insights.claim: Geopolitics inside an international order is treated as a trap that inexorably manufactures conflict from the dualistic mentality that constitutes it, with a geo-civilizational paradigm named as the only exit — while conceding the exit is very far off.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: The author's own conclusion is structurally pessimistic on timeline: conflict-generating dynamics persist for the foreseeable horizon.
insights.quote: What has been a long time gone will be a long time coming.
insights.locator: The trap of geopolitics in an international order

insights.claim: Bruno Maçães' new book for Berggruen Press, 'In Search Of Greater India,' argues pre-nation-state Indian civilization has lessons for the modern West — signalling an institutional push behind the civilizational frame.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Tracks which elite institutions are funding and platforming the civilizational-order narrative.
insights.locator: In his new book for Berggruen Press
